what: Bring Hacker News discussion into prismis the way Reddit's already is, and let a story whose article cannot be fetched be summarized from its discussion, honestly marked as such, for both Hacker News and Reddit, instead of being stored title-only.
why: Hacker News arrives as a plain RSS source (https://news.ycombinator.com/rss), and the RSS fetcher has no comment handling, so a story's discussion is never read; when the linked article is blocked (403 bot walls, Reuters' 401 login wall) the stored content is literally the feed's 'Comments' and the item is title-only: 14 of 234 HN items in the week to 2026-10-10 went title-only on a failed fetch. Reddit appends top comments but its link-without-article rule (readability.py, title-only-misfires) makes a link post with only discussion title-only 'whatever its comments', and the summarizer's substantive check (summarizer.py, SUBSTANTIVE) explicitly calls 'only a link (with or without reader comments)' not substantive. The operator decided on 2026-10-10 that such stories should be summarized from the discussion, marked so it never reads as the article.
decided: Hacker News comments come from HN's official Firebase API (hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/item/<id>.json), whose `kids` are in HN's ranked order (measured: Algolia's items endpoint returns children in id order, not rank); the top N top-level comments are fetched, skipping deleted and dead ones, their HTML converted to plain text.

An RSS entry is a Hacker News story when its comments link is news.ycombinator.com/item?id=<id>; the RSS fetcher enriches exactly those entries, so any HN feed works, and an Ask/Show HN self post (link is the item itself) takes the item's own text as its body.

HN comments are appended under the same discussion header Reddit uses and formatted the same way, capped by a [hackernews] max_comments setting mirroring [reddit] max_comments (default 5), and a failed comment fetch is recorded on the item as comments_outcome, as Reddit does.

An item whose article is missing but whose discussion section has readable prose is readable, with the analysis recording content_basis = "discussion"; with no discussion it stays title-only exactly as today. This replaces the link-without-article rule for both Reddit and HN.

For a discussion-basis item the summarizer is told the article is unavailable and the text is the discussion, writes the summary as a summary of the discussion, and judges `substantive` on whether the discussion says something substantive about the story, not on whether the piece is present.
The reader sees the basis: the TUI reader and the CLI's item view show 'from the discussion — article unavailable' for content_basis = discussion, alongside where title-only is shown today.
HN API calls are tested from recorded vcrpy cassettes like the other third-party HTTP tests.
